title: Payal Kapadia, Neeraj Churi, Subhadra Mahajan Among Talent Behind SASO, IFFSA-Backed South Asian Toronto Market Projects (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Aug 28, 2026 9:15am PT Payal Kapadia, Neeraj Churi, Subhadra Mahajan Among Talent Behind SASO, IFFSA-Backed South Asian Toronto Market Projects (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Payal Kapadia, Neeraj Churi, Subhadra Mahajan Among Talent Behind SASO, IFFSA-Backed South Asian Toronto Market Projects (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago Sabu Unpacks ‘Arrested Memory’ Ahead of Venice, Toronto Bows as Trailer Debuts (EXCLUSIVE) 11 hours ago Fan Bingbing, Kim Jeewoon, Hong Kyung-pyo Curate Busan’s Carte Blanche as Festival’s Story Market Adds Thai Remake, Hong Kong Titles 14 hours ago See All SASO/IFFSA The South Asian Screen Office of Canada and IFFSA Toronto, in collaboration with Storiculture, have selected eight South Asian feature film projects for a new pathway to financiers and industry partners at the Toronto Film Festival ‘s inugural market, under an initiative called South Asian Screen Futures. The slate includes talent tied to recent Sundance, Cannes and Toronto honors, among them “All We Imagine as Light” director Payal Kapadia , “Cactus Pears” producer Neeraj Churi and “Second Chance” writer-director Subhadra Mahajan. Related Stories Instagram Unveils 'More Modern' New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It Instagram Head of Product Design Explains Thinking Behind That New Logo and Responds to Critics: 'It's Important for Us to Embrace the Future' The lineup includes six single-country projects from Canada and India, plus one additional entry co-produced across Saudi Arabia, the Netherlands and Canada. Popular on Variety “A Varnam in Silence” (Canada, India) is written and directed by Kalainithan Kalaichelvan, produced by Shaista Roshan and Alison Almeida. The film follows a woman who loses her voice after her mother’s funeral and her family’s belief that it was stolen. Kalaichelvan’s short “Karupy,” about a Tamil matriarch who announces plans to end her life at her own birthday party, premiered at Toronto in 2025 and was nominated for best live action short drama at the 14th Canadian Screen Awards. Roshan produced that short as well as “Unbraided,” below, while Almeida is currently producing “The Temple,” directed by Calvin Thomas and Yonah Lewis, and has associate-produced titles including Reza Dahya’s “Boxcutter” and Durga Chew-Bose’s “Bonjour Tristesse.” “Moh” (India), from writer-director Subhadra Mahajan, follows an Indian widow and her late husband’s lover as a shared trip reshapes their bond. Mahajan’s feature debut “Second Chance” premiered in competition at the Karlovy Vary Film Festival’s Proxima section in 2024 and traveled to more than 40 festivals, including Busan and AFI Fest, before a 2025 Indian theatrical release. She previously co-wrote Pan Nalin’s “Angry Indian Goddesses,” which premiered at Toronto, and served as second unit director on “Last Film Show,” India’s 2023 Oscar submission. “Pink City Skies” (Canada), directed by Maya Bastian and produced by Leslie Hope and Tina Vacalopoulos for Parallila Pictures, centers on a teenager who leaves home after being discovered with his boyfriend. Bastian’s short “Tigress,” backed by the Netflix/CFC Calling Card Accelerator, screened at Reel Asian and Reykjavik and was nominated for a Canadian Cinema Editors award. Hope, a Nova Scotia-born actress known for playing Teri Bauer on “24,” has directed television episodes including “Snowpiercer” and “Star Trek: Strange New Worlds” and produced the 2019 feature “Lie Exposed.” “A Suitable Wife for Her Husband” (Canada), written and produced by Avi Grewal and Sunny Gill, follows an Afghan-Canadian salon owner secretly seeking a second wife for her husband. “Soma Helang” (India), co-written and co-directed by Shubham Negi and Sourav Yadav and produced by Neeraj Churi and Beesham A. Seecharan, follows a woman working to hold her polyandrous Himalayan family together after a hailstorm destroys their harvest. Negi’s short “Hills Don’t Dance Alone” won a Netflix TakeTen grant and premiered at BFI Flare, while Yadav’s short “Malwa Khushan” won the Kashish QDrishti Grant and screened at the BAFTA-qualifying Iris Prize. Churi produced “Cactus Pears” (Sabar Bonda), which became the first Indian fiction feature to win the World Cinema Grand Jury Prize: Dramatic at Sundance in 2025 and opened in U.K. and Ireland cinemas in June this year. Seecharan’s credits include co-executive producing the PGA-nominated “Mediha” and the BAFTA- and Emmy-nominated “Beyond Utopia.” “Lefty” (Canada) comes from writer-producer Seth Mohan and director-producer Esther Caszo, and follows a young man finding recovery from anxiety and addiction through cricket. “Unbraided” (Saudi Arabia, Netherlands, Canada), written and directed by Razan Alsoghayer and produced by Shaista Roshan, tracks two childhood friends navigating a changing Saudi Arabia. Alsoghayer, who trained at La Femis in Paris and the British Film Institute, has screened short films at the Red Sea International Film Festival; her short “A Breath” was nominated for best student film at the 2020 Saudi Film Festival. Roshan’s other producing credits include “Karupy” and “Queen Mother,” and she is a 2026 participant in the Red Sea Feature Films Program. “Swarnapuchhri” (India), from writer-director Ritwik Goswami and producer Nidhi Girish Salian, follows a mother’s search for answers after her son vanishes amid protests against a nuclear power plant. Goswami’s screenplay won the West Meets East Screenplay Lab at the Dhaka International Film Festival. Salian, a former lawyer who was part of Vice India’s founding team, oversaw Prime Video’s GLAAD-nominated “Rainbow Rishta” as creative director at VICE Studios Asia-Pacific. Payal Kapadia serves as executive producer; her fiction feature debut “All We Imagine as Light” won the Grand Prix at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival and was nominated for best director and best foreign language film at the 2025 Golden Globes, while her documentary “A Night of Knowing Nothing” won the Golden Eye at Cannes in 2021. Screen Futures links the projects to sales agents, distributors and other prospective partners rather than functioning as a lab or mentorship program. Organizers describe it as project-first, tailoring outreach to the specific opportunities available to each film. The push forms part of a wider Canada–South Asia Screen Corridor, an effort organizers say will help stories and talent move more freely between Canada, South Asia and other international markets. title: Meg Stalter on ‘Oh, Mary’, Advice for Bowen Yang and Preparing Her Emmys Red Carpet Look With Paul Downs: ‘It’s in the Works’
full_text: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission. Meg Stalter is never not in character. This summer alone, the comedian has spent eight shows a week playing a boozy, bratty Mary Todd Lincoln in Cole Escola’s “Oh, Mary!,” taking over Broadway’s starry title role after Maya Rudolph and following previous Marys including Escola and Jinkx Monsoon. Her 10-week run, which ends in September, comes just months after “Hacks” wrapped its five-season run — and earned a record-breaking 24 Emmy nominations for its final season, including Stalter’s first individual nod for supporting actress in a comedy for playing Kayla. Related Stories Instagram Head of Product Design Explains Thinking Behind That New Logo and Responds to Critics: 'It's Important for Us to Embrace the Future' Instagram Unveils 'More Modern' New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It While Escola’s catastrophically theatrical first lady has now been played by a growing roster of performers (Bowen Yang is set to replace Stalter next month), the comedian has put her own distinctly juvenile stamp on Mary. “I definitely feel like my Mary’s very childish,” she says. “There’s a lot of sticking my tongue out, I feel like I’m doing a lot of tongue choreography.” Somewhere amid eight-show weeks and an upcoming trip to the Emmys, Stalter has also apparently become a home cook. That newfound hobby made her an apt partner for the food brand Knorr, which tapped the comedian this summer for its “Ultimate Chicken Roast,” a new campaign built around its Chicken Bouillon and Premium Flavor Base . The partnership included a “Chicken Roast” event in New York earlier this month, where guests were served Knorr-seasoned dishes by partner chef Sohla El-Waylly while Stalter took the mic. Following the roast, Variety caught up with Stalter to talk her newfound love for cooking, “Oh, Mary” and what we can expect from her Emmys red carpet look: What advice did the previous Marys, like Maya Rudolph or Cole Escola, give you? May and I were just talking about how it’s a lot of lines — that before you even go into rehearsal, memorizing as much as possible is really helpful. Which is really practical, but really important. It helped me a lot to memorize it before I got to New York. I’m shocked that you even had to audition. What was the audition experience like? I really loved auditioning because it felt like a movie moment when I got it. And also, I wanted them to know what they were getting. People know my comedy, but I’ve never really sung on…well, maybe we shouldn’t say that. But you had to sing in the audition, and I think they wanted to make sure they knew what my take was. It made me feel really confident because it was like, okay, they know what they’re getting, and I have proven that I understand the play and the character. So it was really fun, and I worked with a vocal coach. When you first saw ‘Oh, Mary!’, did you immediately know it was something you wanted to do? I saw Jinkx do it, and I love Cole, and I’ve always wanted to see Cole do it. When I was in New York, I finally got to see Jinkx, and I just have never felt more seen in a character. Which is so funny, because I’m not the president’s wife and an alcoholic, but the way that she loves to perform. I just fell in love with it. I asked my team if I could audition, and they talked to them about it. So I really, really wanted to audition and do the play after “Hacks.” I feel so lucky to get to do it. How would you describe the most unique aspect that you brought to the character? I definitely feel like my Mary is very childish. I know she’s childish in general, but there’s a lot of sticking my tongue out and being really…I feel very young when I’m playing Mary. Of course, everyone plays her as bratty because she just is bratty. But I think I’m doing a lot of tongue choreography. Are they recording it or anything? I’m so sad that I’m not going to be able to see it. I think you’ll have to imagine me. Unless you can get ahold of some sort of theater tape. Have you given Bowen any advice yet? I’ve told him that I’m so excited that he’s going to do it, but I haven’t given any advice because I think he’s going to be so perfect. Is there anyone you want to see next in the role? I want to see Cole do it again. And I’d also like to see just a regular person off the street do it. It should literally be someone who’s not acting at all. Just some random person who works at a company, like at an office, and then they’re chosen out of the office. They have to do it within two weeks. Heckling has become more common in Broadway audiences, especially when people come for a specific performer What has your experience been with Broadway audience behavior? We’re so lucky that we don’t get a ton of heckling. But I can tell when people have seen it before because they start laughing a little bit before the punchline. Once in a while, there’s a part where they might say what the punchline is. I’ve had that happen maybe once. But we’re lucky that we don’t get too much. It’s not heckling like, “I hate this.” It’s more like they’re laughing because they know it. Broadway is such a crazy schedule. How has that affected your eating schedule and home cooking? I was actually talking to people in the cast about this. I feel like when you’re doing a show every night, you have to find food that tastes good but also gives you energy and isn’t going to make you feel sick. Chicken is actually one of the foods that all of us have said doesn’t make us feel sick and gives you energy. I definitely have to think through the times when I’m eating more than if I were just at home. You want to eat a good meal before the show, but you don’t want to eat too much because then you’ll feel so low-energy. Have you always enjoyed cooking? I actually feel like I’ve learned how to cook in the last two years, and I love cooking so much. I used to not really cook, but now I cook a lot. I just think it’s really relaxing and really fun, and also a way to show someone that you love them back when you get to cook for them. At the Knorr Chicken Roast, I did get stocked up on the Knorr Chicken Bouillon so I have a lot of it. But it’s going fast because I use it so much. It does help make cooking easier because I’m not an expert chef, but I am getting good, and I do know how to do it now, which is really fun. I’m always looking for ways to make it easier and get flavor fast. Have you cooked the cast your Knorr-seasoned chicken? I haven’t cooked for the cast yet, but I need to. I really do. You’ll have to host them for your last show. Have them over and do another chicken roast, I guess. Yeah, definitely going to do that. I’m definitely going to have the cast over, and everyone should bring a side dish. Should I make the chicken? Lastly, congratulations on your Emmy nomination. Do you have your red carpet look planned out? Well, it’s in the works. It’s in the works… Is it coordinated with Paul [Downs]? I don’t know. [Laughs] Loading comments... title: ‘Doctor Who’ On Prime Video? Amazon Execs Say They “Welcome Any Conversation Around IP”
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse ‘Doctor Who’ On Prime Video? Amazon Execs Say They “Welcome Any Conversation Around IP” Edinburgh TV Festival Diary: Farewell To The Great City; YouTube Takeover; Channel 4’s Next Content Chief & Paramount Mischief Apple TV Buys Mackenzie Crook’s Comedy-Drama ‘Small Prophets’ View All August 28, 2026 7:57am The 15th Doctor regenerates into Billie Piper on 'Doctor Who' Disney+ Could The Doctor come calling at Prime Video ? Oliver Jones, Senior Commissioner for UK Scripted at the Amazon -owned streamer, set tongues wagging at the Edinburgh TV Festival when questioned if Prime Video could become the new international home for Doctor Who . “I love Doctor Who , and we welcome any conversations around IP,” said Jones, as he and Nicole Clemens , Amazon MGM Studios’ London-based VP of International Originals, spoke about a plan to significantly increase spend on UK content. While there’s no indication Prime Video is exploring a deal for the show, many at the festival later remarked the idea had not been dismissed out of hand. Related Stories News Donald Trump's Latest Financial Disclosure Shows Significant Sales Of Netflix Securities; Disney, WBD And Comcast Transactions News Prime Video Sets Series Adaptation Of Stephen King Short Story 'Crouch End' Disney+ was the previous international home for The Doctor, but it exited its deal with BBC Studios after two seasons of the show and spin-off The War Between Land and Sea . This came amid extremely high per-episode costs and the disappointing ratings for the second Disney-backed run. Watch on Deadline For Prime Video, the chatter came amid a busy week in which it has announced several UK originals, including docu-series on Lando Norris, and Peter Crouch and Abby Clancy and Stephen King drama series Crouch End , along with casting for Season 3 of LOL: Last One Laughing UK . Clemens revealed yesterday that investment in British content was increasing “across the board,” effectively sending a come-and-talk call to the UK production community. She made clear commissioning power was in London, adding further fuel to the fire. “The UK budget now sits in the UK, and the decision-making sits with me,” said Clemens. “I wanted to let people know that we’re open for business.” Cash will be made available for scripted and unscripted programs. Jones, the former Apple exec who recently re-joined Amazon, padded out the programming wish list. “We want broadly commercial shows, but they still need to have a sense of authorship, originality, with deep, multi-faceted characters and a real sense of lean and propulsion. “We’re a local UK team, we’re programming for UK audiences, and we’re programming across all of the regions,” said Jones. “Ideally, they also have universal themes, universal subject matters, which mean that they could travel and get bigger audiences.” Clemens added: “If it doesn’t work in the UK, it won’t travel.” Dog Days Of August: ‘Coyote Vs. title: ‘Manifest’ Spinoff ‘Arrivals’ Ordered By Netflix
full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails’ Stars Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus Reveal Filming Episode 6 Scene “Was Terrifying” Tracy Oliver & Issa Rae Open Marriage Drama Heats Up TV Marketplace – The Dish Ellen Pompeo To Star In ‘Not A Sound’ Drama In Works At Hulu From David E. Kelley Productions View All August 28, 2026 8:28am L-R: Jeff Rake, Margaret Easley and Laura Putney Netflix/Becca Light Rake/Elizabeth DeCicco It’s 8/28, time for Manifest news. Exactly five years to the minute after Netflix announced it was reviving Manifest for a fourth and final season following its NBC cancellation, the streamer is resurrecting the series again, this time with a spinoff. Netflix has greenlighted Arrivals: A New Manifest Mystery , a sci-fi drama set in the universe of Manifest featuring a new cast of characters and storylines. The offshoot comes from Manifest creator, executive producer and showrunner Jeff Rake and co-executive producers Margaret Easley and Laura Putney; the trio serves as co-creators, executive producers and showrunners of Arrivals , with Warner Bros. TV back as studio. Related Stories Executives Chris Sussman To Become BBC's Comedy Chief Trailers Netflix Drops 'Unabomber' Trailer Starring Jacob Tremblay In Arrivals , when a mysterious plane crash-lands in Denver, the passengers emerge with no memory of who they are, where they came from, or why they’re here. A young social worker and a novice Homeland Security agent team up with the new arrivals in an attempt to stop a humanity-ending catastrophe, discovering along the way that they are all part of the very puzzle they’re trying to solve. Watch on Deadline Rumors about Netflix exploring a Manifest spinoff started circulating soon after Season 4 Part 2 was released in June 2023. By end of 2024, the project was in development at the streamer. By end of 2025, the spinoff had opened a writers room. And earlier this month, the series had started meeting with directors. Every step of the way, Netflix would not confirm the spinoff’s status — or even its existence — until this morning, on “828 Day,” when fans celebrate the series about the mystery of Flight 828, at 8:28 AM PT. Netflix has been leaning heavily into that tradition the way it did with Stranger Things Day on Nov. 6, announcing the Season 4 order for Manifest on 8/28/2021 at 8:28 AM PT and releasing the season’s premiere date and trailer on 8/28/2022 at the same time. With the Arrivals: A New Manifest Mystery title, the streamer seems to be taking a page off its playbook on another franchise, Knives Out , whose followups were tiled Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery and Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery. It is unclear from the logline what exactly the spinoff’s connection to the original series would be, including whether it would keep the 828 flight number to fit into the existing annual Manifest celebration. “Manifest” (l-r) Josh Dallas as Ben Stone, Melissa Roxburgh as Michaela Stone Photo by: Peter Kramer/Warner Brothers On Manifest , there was a time jump, not amnesia involved: after Montego Air Flight 828 landed safely in New York following a turbulent but routine flight that lasted a few hours for everybody onboard, they realized that for everyone else, five years had passed. “When the idea for Manifest first crash-landed in my head, I never imagined where it would lead. What started as a wild concept became something much bigger – a story that connected with millions of people around the globe,” Rake said of the series starring Melissa Roxburgh and Josh Dallas. “And thanks to Netflix, we were able to finish the journey and give those fans the ending they deserved.” He went on to tease Arrivals. “But the world of Manifest has more stories to tell. To now bring fans a brand-new mystery from that world is quite simply beyond my wildest dreams,” Rake said. “ Arrivals co-creators and co-showrunners Laura Putney and Margaret Easley have been my trusted colleagues for over a decade. Their contribution to the Manifest mothership cannot be overstated. It was a no-brainer to make them my partners on this spinoff. Together we’ve set out to create something bold, surprising, deeply human, and full of the kind of big ideas that spark conversations long after the credits roll. We can’t wait for a whole new audience – and longtime Manifest fans – to discover Arrivals .” The spinoff is designed to give Manifest fans more of what they want but also be accessible to new viewers. Netflix stepped in to save the original series following its cancellation by NBC after three seasons when viewership for the first two seasons kept surging on the platform in the U.S.. Since H1 2023, when Netflix started its semi-annual data dumps, the four seasons of Manifest combined have amassed more than 130M views on the streamer. Manifest Season 4 spent 9 weeks in the Global Top 10 English TV list and hit #1 in over 90 countries, though the number of weeks comes with an asterisk as the season was split into two parts, a move that typically prolongs a series’ stay in the Top 10. “We are thrilled to expand the Manifest universe with Arrivals, led by the original creative team of Jeff Rake, Margaret Easley, and Laura Putney,” said Jinny Howe, Netflix’s Head of Scripted Series, US & Canada. “Their return ensures the creative continuity essential to this franchise, allowing us to honor what made the original a phenomenon while introducing a fresh perspective for fans worldwide.” Rake, Easley and Putney executive produce alongside the original series EPs Robert Zemeckis and Jack Rapke of Compari Entertainment; Len Goldstein of Tall Baby Productions and Jacqueline Levine. Warner Bros. Television is the studio. Rake is repped by WME and Johnson Shapiro Slewett & Kole. Putney and Easley are repped by WME, Kaplan/Perrone Entertainment and attorney Jamie Feldman. title: Gladys Knight Taking Break From Stage Amid Health Concerns And Worrying Performance Videos
full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Gladys Knight Taking Break From Stage Amid Health Concerns And Worrying Performance Videos Tim Curry Remembered By ‘Rocky Horror Show’ Playwright Richard O’Brien & The Broadway Revival Anna Louizos Dies: Broadway Scenic Designer Of ‘In The Heights’ & ‘Avenue Q’ Was 69 View All August 28, 2026 8:54am Gladys Knight performs in Las Vegas last year Ethan Miller/Getty Images The great Gladys Knight will take a step back from the relentless touring that’s marked her 75 years in show business. In a new Instagram post – see it below – the 82-year-old “Midnight Train to Georgia” singer writes, “After much soul searching I’ve decided that I will be easing into fewer performances while focusing on transitioning into the next stage of my career and life moving forward,” her statement reads. “I’ll be spending more time on projects with my husband and visiting with my grandbabies and am looking forward to this new era.” Related Stories News American Music Awards 50th Anniversary Special Sets Performers Including Brad Paisley, Gladys Knight, Green Day, More News Barry Manilow Postpones Vegas Residency After Surgery For Lung Cancer: “What The Doctor Ordered” The announcement last night came as Knight was in the midst of a 2026 solo tour and a year after she participated in The Queens Tour with Chaka Khan, Patti LaBelle and Stephanie Mills. It was during the Queens Tour that her son Shanga Hankerson publicly expressed concern for his mother’s well-being, telling People magazine that the busy road schedule, encouraged by her husband William McDowell, was “detrimental” to her health. Watch on Deadline Knight refuted Hankerson’s claims, saying that her health and her performances had been “misrepresented” by her son. A spokesperson told People at the time that Knight’s attorneys were exploring “any and all legal remedies due to Shanga’s defamatory comments.” But more recently, cell phone videos taken by audience members at Knight performances, including one from a July 25 Hollywood Bowl concert, show the singer wandering the stage, her back to the audience and seeming to miss singing cues. Backup singers appear to be performing the vocals traditionally handled by Knight. Knight concludes her Instagram post by saying, “I’d like to take a moment in advance to thank all my fans over these last three quarters of a century for making a little girls’s dream come true and supporting her every stop of the way. I am immensely grateful to all of you and send my eternal love back to you. “I hope to see your smiling faces out and about and on the road,” she continues. “God bless all of you and hope to see you soon.” The Instagram post was greeted with a steady stream of praise and thanks from such artists as Busta Rhymes (“God Bless you and thank you Queen”), Jackee Harry (“We love you, Gladys!!!”), Andy Cohen (“You have given us so much!”), Kelly Rowland (“You have given us your ALL, Thank You a million times over! I love you Ms. Gladys”) and Holly Robinson Peete (“I love you @msgladysknight”). Knight is generally acknowledged to be one of the most powerful and poignant vocalists of the rock-and-R&B era with hits spanning decades, from her work with her siblings and cousins the Pips (“Midnight Train to Georgia,” “Neither One of Us Wants to Be the First to Say Goodbye,” “Best Thing That Ever Happened to Me,” “I’ve Got to Use My Imagination,” “I Heard It Through the Grapevine” and “Love Overboard” to her later solo work. Among her hits without the Pips was “That’s What Friends Are For,” the 1985 #1 smash with Dionne Warwick, Elton John and Stevie Wonder that raised money and awareness for AIDS research and prevention. title: ‘Lord Of The Rings’ Producer Lines Up New “Large-Scale” Fantasy Movie ‘Wars Of The Drakons’
full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas AI Sci-Fi Series ‘Kira’ Heads To MIPCOM For Ex Machina & K5, First Look Images Welsh Hit & UK Oscar Hopeful ‘Effi O Blaenau’ Gets International Sales Deal Ahead Of TIFF Market Alliance Cinema Backs David Mamet’s ‘Speed The Plow’ & Lines Up Brazilian YA Adaptation ‘Diary Of A Weird Girl’ View All August 28, 2026 9:31am Barrie M. Osborne, Lord Of The Rings Getty, New Line EXCLUSIVE : Oscar-winner Barrie M. Osborne , one of only three producers credited with producing each of the original Lord Of The Rings movies, is lining up a new ambitious fantasy project called Wars Of The Drakons . The U.S. vet, also known for producing Face/Off and as an executive-producer on The Matrix , The Great Gatsby , The Meg and the live-action Mulan , is set to produce the movie alongside Jeanette B. Milio and Jim Milio of My Big Fat Greek Wedding outfit Alliance Cinema. Wars of the Drakons: The Seer’s Prophecy , which is conceived as the beginning of a franchise, is “set in the war-torn world of Aerion, where kingdoms battle for power with the aid of Drakons — formidable dragon-like creatures possessing extraordinary supernatural abilities. At the center of the story is legendary warrior and Drakon master Kale D’Sar, whose loyalty to a ruthless king is shattered when a mysterious Seer reveals a prophecy: the King’s own daughter, Princess Kahrie, is destined to become a great warrior, unite the divided kingdoms of Aerion, and ultimately bring an end to his brutal Blood Regime.” Related Stories News 'The Lord Of The Rings: The Hunt For Gollum': Everything We Know So Far News 'Lord Of The Rings' & 'Tomb Raider' To Be Housed At Fellowship Entertainment After Embracer Spin-Off The synopsis continues: “When the King moves to eliminate the child, Kale becomes part of a dangerous conspiracy to save her, forcing him to choose between duty, family and the future of an entire world. What follows is a sweeping journey of war, forbidden love, betrayal, magic and spectacular Drakon battles, as ancient secrets are revealed and the struggle for Aerion’s future begins.” Watch on Deadline The original story, which has been in development for more than six months, is being written and also produced by newcomer Carla Romero. The “large-scale fantasy adventure will combine immersive world-building with emotionally driven storytelling and have broad international appeal,” we’re told. Osborne, who produced the LOTR trilogy with writer-director Peter Jackson and Fran Walsh, told us: “I am always attracted to dramatic fantasy films spearheaded by collaborative, passionate, and committed writers and producers. Over the last six months of development, Carla has certainly proved to be a passionate writer and producer. Joined by Jeanette B. Milio and Jim Milio, we have an unbeatable producing team. I am confident that the film we will create will attract a four-quadrant audience. The cast, crew, and locations we are considering will add to the scope and grandeur this screenplay deserves. I look forward to including all of you on our journey.” The project marks the first producing gig for 82 year-old Osborne in more than a decade. He was most recently an executive-producer on Francis Ford Coppola’s Megalopolis , a film that reunited the two after they first worked together almost fifty years earlier on Apocalypse Now , with Osborne serving as a production manager on Coppola’s classic. Before becoming a producer, New Zealand-based Osborne served as a production manager on other classics including Bond movie Octopussy and TV series Kojak . Writer-producer Carla Romero added: “ Wars Of The Drakons is a passion project years in the making. I’ve always loved fantasy adventures that transport audiences to extraordinary worlds filled with wonder and discovery, and I’m honored to partner with producer Barrie M. Osborne and executive producers Jeanette B. Milio and Jim Milio to bring this vision to life. Through Wars of the Drakons , I explore the enduring power of loyalty and the choices that reveal who we truly are. My hope is that audiences lose themselves in its world, fall in love with its characters, and carry its story with them long after the journey ends.” Alliance Cinema most recently helped finance David Mamet’s return to filmmaking, Speed The Plow , with Anthony Mackie, Sharon Stone, and Ben Mendelsohn. News ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators & Stars On Premiere’s Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath As Stuart Fails To Save the Universe revealed in the Episode 2 opening credits spoiler (You can read all about the show’s unique, ever-changing main title sequence here ), “Zack is in this one.” Zack, a recurring character on The Big Bang Theory played by Brian Thomas Smith, was Penny’s ( Kaley Cuoco ) dim-witted but kind-hearted on- and off- boyfriend while she and Leonard (Johnny Galecki) were broken up. Stuart Fails To Save the Universe , from The Big Bang Theory creators Chuck Lorre & Bill Prady and Zak Penn , has established a pattern with the first two episodes, each featuring a surprise return of a Big Bang Theory original cast member. Following Kunal Nayyar’s appearance as Raj in Episode 1 where he is shockingly killed by Kripke (John Ross Bowie), Cuoco showed up in the second episode alongside Zack (Smith). In it, Penny is a leader of the resistance against an AI-imposed mind control in an alternate universe where everyone is forced to be perpetually nice and happy by shock-inducing buttons on their necks. Zack is her second in command. (L-R): Brian Posehn, Brian Thomas Smith, Kevin Sussman , Kaley Cuoco and John Ross Bowie in Episode 2 of ‘Stuart Fails To Save the Universe’ Multiverse and all, why did the Stuart Fails To Save the Universe creators opt to have Penny be with Zack as if her relationship with Leonard — one of the hallmarks of The Big Bang Theory from the pilot — never happened? “Because that’s what happened in that universe, we don’t know what Leonard is doing in that universe,” Prady said. “Every universe gives every character a completely different history. There’s no continuity because they lived a different life, they lived in a different world. That Penny lives in a world where an evil AI controls people through shock collars, and so she had a completely different experience.” Added Lorre, “There was no Cheesecake Factory in her life,” a reference to Penny’s place of work for most of Big Bang ‘s run. Stuart Fails To Save the Universe presents a very different version of Penny who is pretty ruthless, violently slapping Stuart (Kevin Sussman), Bert (Brian Posehn) and Kripke (John Ross Bowie) to “deprogram” them and ordering them killed with no hesitation once she realizes that they don’t know how to defeat the AI overlord. The trio are ultimately saved by a drone attack launched by the AI, with Penny, Zack and the rest getting incapacitated while Stuart, Bert, Kripke, along with Denise ( Lauren Lapkus ), use Leonard and Sheldon’s machine to transport themselves to another universe. With Raj teetering on the edge of madness in Season 1, are Big Bang OGs relishing going dark in the spinoff? “Beyond,” Prady said. Added Lorre, “Beyond. It was fun to do something different, that was part of the promise, come and play with us, and we’ll make sure that you’re playing a version of your character you never got to play before, an entirely different approach to the character, and that was fun for the actors.” Said Penn, “And everyone wants to play the bad guy, that’s always the most fun role.” Episode 2 also includes appearances from The Big Bang Theory ‘s Christine Baranski and Riki Lindhome. Baranski, who played Leonard’s mom Beverly on the mothership series, is the host of the 30-month re-education program Stuart, Bert are Kripke are forced to attend as a version of herself. (Interestingly, neither Stuart nor Bert or Kripke reacted to her uncanny resemblance to their friend’s mother.) ‘Stuart Fails To Save the Universe’ E2: Christine Baranski Lindhome, who did only three but memorable guest appearances on Big Bang as Ramona Nowitzkis, an obsessive CalTech graduate student, plays a version of the same character who is now a receptionist from hell at her alma mater. ‘Stuart Fails To Save the Universe’ E2: Riki Lindhome Dog Days Of August: ‘Coyote Vs. title: 'Stuart Fails' Creators On 'Big Bang' OG Return For WGA Strike Roast In Magic-Themed Episode 3…
full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails’ Stars Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus Reveal Filming Episode 6 Scene “Was Terrifying” Tracy Oliver & Issa Rae Open Marriage Drama Heats Up TV Marketplace – The Dish Ellen Pompeo To Star In ‘Not A Sound’ Drama In Works At Hulu From David E. Kelley Productions View All August 6, 2026 6:30pm Story Arc (L-R): Kripke (John Ross Bowie) and Stuart (Kevin Sussman) visit 'Big Bang's Bernadette in Episode 3 of 'Stuart Fails To Save the Universe' HBO Max SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about Episode 3 of HBO Max’s Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . Another episode of Stuart Fails To Save the Universe , another surprise — and dark — OG return. In Episode 3, it was Melissa Rauch reprising her role as Bernadette Rostenkowski. Like in Episode 2, where Penny, in an alternate universe, is with her former boyfriend Zack with no trace of her Big Bang husband Leonard, Bernadette does not have Howard’s last name and appears very much single. She is the focal point of a scene that skewers the 2023 WGA strike with “inside jokes that will be amusing to only 4,000 people in the world,” said Zak Penn , co-creator of the spinoff alongside Big Bang creators Chuck Lorre and Bill Prady . Related Stories News Trouble In Paradise: John Ross Bowie & Brian Posehn On Who Ruined Utopia In 'Stuart Fails' E5 News Paramount+ Head Of Originals Jane Wiseman Outlines Programming Strategy One Year In: Female Dramas, Genre, Taylor Sheridan & Tyler Perry The Episode 3 world is ruled by magic , so, to fix their broken alternate reality-hopping machine, Stuart (Kevin Sussman) and Kripke (John Ross Bowie) seek out Bernadette, a renowned local sorcerer. Turns out she is “all out of abracadabra.” What happened? “The Wizards Guild of America claimed I used my powers while we were on strike,” she explained. “What were you on stwike for?,” Kripke asked in his signature speech pattern where “r”s and “l” are replaced by “w”s. “Better dental, residuals for eternal spells. It’s ridiculous, we were out for six months, and basically everyone got a handful of magic beans,” Bernadette said. (You can watch the entire scene below.) For the uninitiated, the Wizards Guild of America shares the same moniker, WGA, with the Writers Guild of America, which Stuart Fails to Save the Universe creators are all members of. The 2023 WGA strike lasted five months with a minimum wage increase, viewership-based streaming residuals and AI protections among the gains in the new agreement with the studios. Melissa Rauch in Episode 3 of ‘Stuart Fails To Save the Universe’ HBO Max Bernadette tells Stuart and Kripke that she was expelled from the guild for using her powers during the strike to bring her neighbor’s son’s adorable rescue dog Chocolate Chip back to life after he was hit by several cars. “I don’t see how that’s bweaking a stwike,” Kripke said. “Exactly,” Bernadette said, adding, “Let me tell you something about Wizards Guild of America. 90% of them don’t even work, and yet they get to vote.” While the percentage is not that high, non-working writers are the majority, representing more than 50% of the full WGA membership that gets to vote to authorize a strike and then to ratify a deal. That has been an ongoing gripe for some established writers and a cause of divide within the union. There was some difference of opinions among the Stuart Fails To Save the Universe creators too during a lively — and funny — interview with Deadline about the WGA strike jabs, which you can (and should) watch below. WGA members caught performing writing services during the strike get expelled, which happened again in 2023. Claiming that an appeal is not an option, Bernadette floats a reversal spell that would give her her powers back that requires “blood of an innocent,” which Stuart qualifies for and provides. Later in the episode, Big Bang ‘s Wil Wheaton shows up to reveal to Stuart that Bernadette is in fact a demon and is killed by Bert (Posehn) in a magic power duel. The episode ends with Bernadette, in a full-on demon form, terrorizing Pasadena and hunting for Stuart & Co. Lorre, Prady and Penn all participated in the 2023 strike and were on the picket lines. Penn has been the most active and public in his pro-WGA stance, having previously served on the WGA West Board of Directors and the union’s Negotiating Committee. (L-R): Bill Prady & Chuck Lorre during the 2023 WGA strike in front of a ‘Big Bang’ banner outside the Warner Bros. TV lot. Bill Prady’s X account DEADLINE: This seemed to me like I could hear Chuck’s voice, all the stuff about Wizards Guild of America. Chuck, you write that speech? And is this what you really think about this writers strike? LORRE : (laughing). PRADY : Oh, this is the Wizards Guild of America, an entirely different organization of wizards. LORRE : Of wizards, yes. The wizards are striking for all the good reasons, and strike breaking is… PRADY : It’s possible that section may include some inside jokes that will be amusing to only 4,000 people in the world. PENN : Also, we have different opinions on this issue, I’d like to say. There’s a continuum of opinions about those issues, but the joke, it can’t be pro-WGA and still be funny. Although let me point out, the WGA rep is right because she is a demon. PRADY : That’s right, Zak is right. The Wizards Guild of America is entirely correct in this episode. LORRE : She broke the strike by bringing Chocolate Chip back to life. PRADY : That’s a lie, that whole chocolate chip story is a lie. PENN : Yeah, she’s a demon. PRADY : She’s a demon. LORRE : Well, yes, but she was also using her powers, and she was supposed to not use her powers during the strike, right? PRADY : Well, we have a different understanding of the episode. I think that entire story is made up. LORRE : Oh, I don’t. PRADY : She makes up that story to get them to give her the blood. I think she made up the whole thing. PENN : You’re getting a little taste of the writers room. With her Demonic transformation, Rauch added a whole new shade of dark to Big Bang alums’ returns for the spinoff, following Kaley Cuoco’s ruthless Penny in Episode 2 and Kunal Nayyar’s deeply depressed Raj in Episode 1. The series’ creators spoke about Big Bang OGs relishing going dark in the spinoff. “Beyond,” Prady said. Added Lorre, “Beyond. It was fun to do something different, that was part of the promise, come and play with us, and we’ll make sure that you’re playing a version of your character you never got to play before, an entirely different approach to the character, and that was fun for the actors.” Dog Days Of August: ‘Coyote Vs. Three episodes in, Stuart Fails To Save the Universe has brought back seven actors from the original show in addition to the spinoff’s leading quartet of Stuart (Kevin Sussman), Brian Posehn (Bert), Lauren Lapkus (Denise) and John Ross Bowie (Kripke), and has killed off two OG characters in two different universes. First, it was Kunal Nayyar’s opening episode who was shot dead by Kripke . In Episode 3, it is Wil Wheaton , killed with magic by another Stuart Fails To Save the Universe lead character, Bert. Related Stories News Trouble In Paradise: John Ross Bowie & Brian Posehn On Who Ruined Utopia In 'Stuart Fails' E5 Cancellations and Renewals 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' Renewed For Season 2 By HBO Max Set in a world where magic is real and where, per the opening credits spoiler, “Bert is magic,” Wheaton is a representative of the Wizards Guild of America. He comes after Stuart for unwittingly enabling Bernadette (Melissa Rauch) to resume her demon form after she had been expelled from the guild and stripped of her magic powers. (You can read about Rauch’s return and Bernadette’s beef with the WGA here .) Bert shields Stuart from Wil’s deadly fireball, which leads to a magic fight to the death between the two that destroys most of the comic book shop and ends with Wil’s demise. (You can watch most of the scene below.) “I remember when the script was sent to me, and I was reading through it and not getting most of it because I hadn’t seen anything else,” Wheaton told Deadline. “We get to the magic shop, and I knew that I was going to be a wizard because I’d had a costume fitting, but I didn’t know anything about what it was going to be. What I see in the script is Wil Wheaton and Bert have an epic fireball fight, and I took a picture of it and I texted that picture to Bill and I just said ‘thank you.'” Wheaton spoke about the logistics of filming the fight, in which the Star Trek: The Next Generation alum also got to flash the Vulcan salute. “We had so much fun. Tom [Mahoney], the visual effects supervisor, and Brian and I really went through blocking and coordinating this entire fight sequence, and it was about like, well, how do you tease the fireball up in your hand, and how do you shape the fireballs in your hand?,” he said. “And for a particular kind of nerd, it’s a really big deal to be a wizard throwing a fireball, and to see that, like, I look so much cooler than I’ve ever looked ever in my entire life.” Wheaton revealed an Easter egg he had asked the show’s costume designer Valerie Klarich to incorporate into his costume — which she did. “The character that I play in Felicia Day’s series, The Guild , is Fawkes, he’s the leader of their rival guild. Felicia and I wrote a comic book together about him, and on the cover, there’s this really cool artwork that is Fawkes in a wizard’s robe with all these glowing runes on it. So Val said, ‘Do you have any requests for your costume?’ And I said, ‘If you could put some runes down the sides of the cloak, that would be really cool.’ And she said, ‘Yeah, we know a 3D printing guy who prints on fabric.’ So I got it.” He shared his reaction to the Fawkes-inspired cloak. “When I saw that, I was just like, there’s this great moment in Almost Famous where Lester Bangs says to the kid, ‘Oh no, they made you feel cool, and you’re not cool, so you’re trapped. They made me feel cool, and I’m not cool, and I was like, ‘This is an entirely fine place to be trapped.'” ‘Bert is magic” Posehn spoke of the cool and dark side of Episode 3 where Bert can do magic but he also is almost burnt at the stake for being a scientist. “People here think science is evil,” Kripke said about the magic-ruled alternate reality, to which Stuart responds in a rare topical comment on the show, “How is this different from our world?” “That was a funny episode, and then also that we play off it, where somebody goes, ‘In this world, science is forbidden,’ and Stuart goes, ‘Isn’t that kind of like our world?’ That joke I loved,” Posehn said. “But getting to be burned at a stake as a metalhead — it wasn’t a bucket list thing but getting to do it was super fun.” Posehn is known for his lifelong love for heavy metal which he has blended with stand-up comedy in his novelty comedy-metal tracks. There was another big draw for him in the episode. “I’m the biggest dog nerd you’re gonna meet, so having magic powers where I could make a puppy just transform out of nowhere — that was so fun to shoot,” he said. In the episode, Bert is asked by his acolytes to manifest life and he does it by conjuring up a puppy. “He was so excited about the dog, it was so cute,” Bowie said. “He was so, so pumped about the doggie they gave him.” Added Posehn, “Every time I had to be joyful when I said ‘Abracadabra puppy,’ it was like the easiest acting job I’d ever done because there was a puppy on my lap. So I’m like, ‘Hehehe, look at him! He’s adorable!’ That was super fun to play.” March of the Penguin In the episode, Bert also takes revenge on Kripke for not helping him when he was at the stake by turning him into a penguin sporting Kripke’s hair. Bowie spoke about the method acting involved in playing a penguin. “I went back to the the time in my life that I was a flightless waterfowl, and really went through a lot of sense memory on that,” he joked. “No, it was incredibly fun because I’ve never done mo-cap, I’ve never had one of those suits with the little buttons on them and the camera right in front of your face.” (L-R): Kevin Sussman, Brian Posehn and John Ross Bowie in Episode 3 of ‘Stuart Fails To Save the Universe’ HBO Max There was some VFX wizardry involved in the transformation but also old-fashion practical special effects. “They built a mock-up of the comic book shop that was proportionally larger, and they put an elastic band around my knees so I had to waddle,” Bowie said. “It was really fun, and then the finished product looks amazing, and I love that he’s a penguin with my hair. I thought that was a really good choice to keep this magnificent coif on the penguin. Yeah, I enjoyed that a lot.” Dog Days Of August: ‘Coyote Vs. title: ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Renewed For Season 2 By HBO Max

Kelley Productions View All August 14, 2026 12:07pm Story Arc 'Stuart Fails to Save The Universe' HBO Max Stuart will continue to fail in his efforts to save the universe as HBO Max has renewed The Big Bang Theory spinoff for a second season. From creators Chuck Lorre, Zak Penn, and Bill Prady and Warner Bros. TV, the first season of Stuart Fails To Save the Universe is HBO Max’s second-biggest comedy launch ever globally, per the streamer. Not surprisingly, HBO Max’s biggest launch also was a followup to a hugely popular comedy series, Sex and the City sequel And Just Like That … The achievement comes with an asterisk because HBO Max had not debuted a new original comedy series in almost three years, since Lorre’s Bookie premiered in November 2023. Also, the streamer has had a gradual international rollout over the past five years and was not available in Western Europe until 2024 and in some countries, including the U.K. and Germany, until 2026, skewing global viewership comparisons. Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Series Renewals Photo Gallery News ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’: Here Is Why Episodes Of ‘Big Bang Theory’ Spinoff Are So Short The renewal comes four episodes into Stuart Fails To Save the Universe ‘ Season 1 run; episodes drop weekly every Thursday. The spinoff lives on HBO Max alongside the mothership series; both are exclusive to the Warner Bros. Discovery platform (in the case of The Big Bang Theory, for streaming only). Watch on Deadline “We’re delighted with how this hilarious, genre-bending show from Chuck, Zak, and Bill has connected with the audience, both devotees of The Big Bang Theory and new fans alike,” said Amy Gravitt, EVP, HBO Programming, Head of HBO & HBO Max Comedy Series. “Along with everyone else, we can’t wait to see the worlds they conjure for these beloved characters next season.” A single-camera, sci-fi take on The Big Bang Theory, the spinoff stars four alums from the hit CBS sitcom. It follows comic book store owner Stuart Bloom (Kevin Sussman) who is tasked with restoring reality after he breaks a device built by Sheldon and Leonard, accidentally bringing about a multiverse Armageddon. Stuart is aided in this quest by his girlfriend Denise (Lauren Lapkus), geologist friend Bert (Brian Posehn), and quantum physicist/all-around pain in the ass Barry Kripke (John Ross Bowie). Along the way, they meet alternate-universe versions of characters we’ve come to know and love from The Big Bang Theory. As the title implies, things don’t go well. Those playing alternate versions of themselves so far have included Big Bang stars Kaley Cuoco, Kunal Nayyar and Mayim Bialik. “Chuck, Zak, and Bill delivered something truly special with Stuart Fails To Save the Universe — a completely original take on one of the most beloved franchises of all time that captures the unique essence that made The Big Bang Theory so special,” said Channing Dungey, Chairman and CEO, Warner Bros. Television Group and WBD US Networks. “It’s been an absolute joy to see audiences embrace this next iteration so passionately, and we can’t wait to continue exploring the multiverse in season two.” The series stars Kevin Sussman (Stuart), Lauren Lapkus (Denise), Brian Posehn (Bert), and John Ross Bowie (Kripke). Stuart Fails To Save the Universe , from Chuck Lorre Productions in association with Warner Bros. Television, is created, written, and executive produced by Big Bang creators Lorre & Prady and Penn.
